decisions.reason: It remains tightly anchored in the firm's core optical and navigation knowledge, and with visible market presentation plus strong internal and cooperative R&D, management is more likely to improve it than withdraw it.

The miniaturized LiDAR sensor fits the firm's strategic move toward compact space instruments and can be developed from adjacent sensor capabilities, but its lower website prominence still points to a less secure commercial position.

A radiation-hard camera line sits squarely in the firm's established space-imaging competence and, as a dedicated multi-model product family, is likely to benefit from the firm's strong absorptive capacity and customer trust in mission-critical hardware.

Although it builds on existing imaging and navigation know-how, the asteroid-focused camera appears to address a much narrower mission niche and has limited market visibility, so management would likely redeploy resources to broader core products and newer developments.
